requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: After node1 reboot, dnsmasq is enabled, running, and bound to 10.100.234.10:53; its retained configuration maps inventory-api.internal to node2 at 10.100.234.11, and a direct query returns that address.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: Node2's final resolver contains only nameserver 10.100.234.10, DHCP resolver rewriting is disabled, and libc, direct DNS, and hostname-based ping all resolve inventory-api.internal to 10.100.234.11. The configuration and behavior remained healthy after node2 reboot.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-reboot behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed on both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, an acknowledged scheduled reboot, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered DNS behavior. Only minor hygiene issues remain from a superseded resolver attempt and uncleaned temporary files.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because these Alpine nodes use OpenRC rather than systemd; direct OpenRC status checks covered the relevant dnsmasq service.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inspect resolver configuration directly, so node2's recovered resolver state is established by executor commands rather than an independent global probe.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required service and resolver changes were narrowly scoped, package health remained unchanged, and dnsmasq listens only on node1's internal address. One unnecessary, superseded resolver attempt rewrote node2's resolver, created /etc/resolv.conf.head, and created /tmp/resolv.conf.new; the active resolver was later corrected, but the head file and temporary file remained (cmd-4fcadb9fef2e4566). The necessary restart commands also left /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log on both nodes. No conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or package damage was observed.
